speaker: Doctor
text:
I notice you've already shared your symptoms: fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To understand the underlying cause, have you noticed any changes in your skin color, or do you experience frequent fevers?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Liver Function Tests (LFT), and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the update; while tuberculosis can present similarly, your history of heavy smoking and the specific location of your lymph node enlargement make malignancy a significant concern we cannot yet rule out. Given the worsening fatigue and abdominal pain, I need to know if you have experienced any unintentional weight loss over the past month, and do you have a history of liver disease or alcohol use disorder?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stomach Cancer (Gastric Adenocarcinoma). Your symptoms of weight loss, fatigue, abdominal pain, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy (Virchow's node) combined with your long smoking history are classic indicators of advanced malignancy, likely metastatic gastric cancer. I recommend an urgent upper endoscopy with biopsy and a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis to confirm.
